title: The 3.7.0 changelog
desiredOutcome: CHANGELOG.md's unreleased section describes every user-visible change since 3.6.0

findings.issue: The ### Fixed entry reports a defect that no release ever had. It says the state commit 'asked the assembled plan whether it was sharded ... so it never took the lock'. But `commit-task-work.py --state` does not exist at 0dfae3e7 (v3.6.0): `git show 0dfae3e7:plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-task-work.py` has no "--state", and the retired `commit-manifest-index.py` did take the index lock. `index_is_sharded` first appears in 52c80676, inside this same unreleased window, as a fix to the P142.1 verb. A reader on 3.6.0 would conclude they ran a lockless state commit. That is a claim about released behaviour the code history does not support.
findings.resolution: Drop the ### Fixed section and fold its content into the existing 'One commit verb' / Removed entries as what the verb does: `--state` takes the index lock in a sharded plan (it asks the index file on disk, and a file it cannot read counts as sharded), commits the shard from the bytes its index part was derived from, makes a root commit on a branch with no commit yet, and under `--json` keeps stdout one object with the lock's lines on stderr and a refusal carrying its `lockCode`.

findings.issue: The non-UTF-8 path entry sits under ### Changed and says the drive 'now' reads such paths and, 'on Windows', compares them itself. `_git_path` and `_literal_matches` do not exist at 0dfae3e7; they were added by 1d95127f and a5f42ae9 with the recut and carry machinery, and 3bcd5772 only reworked them. So there is no 3.6.0 behaviour to have changed. Also `_changed_between` and `_unheld` now call `_literal_matches` on every platform, not only Windows, so 'on Windows' under-describes where the comparison happens.
findings.resolution: Fold the sentence into the recut / kept-tree entries as a property of reading a tree's work, and say the paths are compared by the drive rather than handed to git as pathspecs, with Windows named as the reason rather than the scope.

findings.issue: 'a plan that could not be read gets nothing forced' is true only for a key that is not a redo's aside key. `_kept_tree_remedy` tests `_is_aside_key` first, so an aside-key tree gets `git worktree remove --force` and the save-first commands even when `task_ids` is None. The sentence follows 'offered to that kind of tree alone', which makes the unreadable-plan case read as covering that kind too.
findings.resolution: Say that a key which is neither a redo's nor a task of the plan, and any key when the plan could not be read, gets nothing forced (an unreadable plan offers `task-remove` only, once it reads).

findings.issue: 'the fix run ... has the recorded cost of those suites held back from the runs before it' omits that `sweep_budget` caps the reserve at half the deadline (`min(recorded, timeout // 2)`). With a heavy suite the held-back share is not the recorded cost.
findings.resolution: Add 'up to half the deadline' (a word, no numeral) after 'held back'.

findings.issue: 'exit 1 with a `ROW NOT PROVEN:` line per row ... which stops the sign-off quoting each' - `lint_probe` quotes at most five (`rows[:5]`). Minor over-statement. Cosmetic: the start-charge entry has a short, awkwardly wrapped line ('running when. A repeated row for a state already reached folds').
findings.resolution: Say 'quoting the rows' and rewrap the start-charge entry.

review.outcome: [findings: 5 - 0 high, 1 med, 4 low; 0 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: The CHANGELOG's unreleased section describes every user-visible change since 3.6.0
tasks.description: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] covers only P142.1 (the one commit verb) and its Removed entry. Before 3.7.0 is cut, add, in the house style of earlier sections (### Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed, bold lead sentence, prose after), every user-visible change the plugin (plugins/audit/) landed since v3.6.0: read `git log --no-merges --format='%h %s' v3.6.0..HEAD -- plugins/audit` and each commit's diff and write each line from what landed, not from its title. Expected areas: sign-off runs the full gate once and probes a guarded lint only when the phase changed it, the lint probe named by the plan and bounded; red-first through a sweep-shaped command (passing suites with new cases red at HEAD, a suite file missing at HEAD, deadline sized from recorded cost); runner output normalised so CRLF from a Windows pipe is read the same everywhere; task trees following the phase head, recut with their work, never destroyed without proof they hold no work (redo keeps the old tree under a kept marker, one forced-removal function), and status advice naming what --force destroys; start-task charge accounting (repeated and echoed status rows); build commands that run at sign-off not defaulted into a phase gate; agent session temp cleanup; the state commit taking the index lock and committing on an unborn branch; the drive's Windows path handling (non-UTF-8 names). Tooling outside plugins/audit (tools/, tests/, ci.yml, prove-gates, sweep sharding) is not user-visible and gets no line. Keep the existing two entries; merge rather than duplicate. No number written into prose (`_output_lints.prose_number_claims` and `_deps.doc_prose_numbers` must stay empty); no F/P/BUG ids. Acceptance: every user-visible plugin change since v3.6.0 has a line; the prose lints are empty.
